assets.title: Harappa: an older route beneath later encroachment
assets.caption: Period 2 cart-track centre-lines are transferred onto the upper street drawing using independent excavation-grid controls. The source identifies later paving and an encroachment drain in this corridor. The drawings provide a location relation but no matched internal-wall survival denominator.

assets.title: Harappa: a drain replaced part of a gateway
assets.caption: The Mound ET gateway drawing combines several building stages. The report places a later corbelled drain through the older gateway after three earlier western drains ceased to function; an east-west street crossed above the culvert. Access changed while the drainage system was rebuilt.

assets.title: Dholavira: successive additions to the same defence
assets.caption: The source schematic section orders the Castle defence and later deposits across seven stages. The report describes an 11 m basal wall in Stage I, a 2.8 m inward addition in Stage II and a 4.5 m addition in Stage III. These are published section dimensions; the schematic is not used for a new metre estimate.

assets.caption: The report photographs an arterial street and separately describes a Stage V wall encroaching on an earlier 5.25 m street in trench 15x24. This photograph has no surveyed link to that trench, so no particular wall is marked as the encroachment and no remaining width is estimated.

assets.title: Dholavira: a water connection with unresolved phases
assets.caption: The Castle plan links a well to two tanks and shows solid and dashed channel segments. assets.title: Lothal: a Phase IV passage and entrance
assets.caption: Rao’s Phase IV Block B plan supplies two measurable openings: a passage about 1.1 m wide and the northern entrance of house 172.IVa about 2.2 m wide. They describe local access geometry in one phase. The earlier matched block plan and the whole-town street plate remain unavailable.

assets.title: Lothal: one drain, several kinds of drawing
assets.caption: The public-drain illustration combines an isometric view, a section and a plan of drain 15A. It identifies a cesspool, damaged masonry and sockets interpreted by the source as fittings for a wooden screen. The multiple projections and missing phase key prevent a direct before-and-after persistence measure.

assets.title: Harappa: walls, streets and a later channel cut
assets.caption: The paired plan and section place curtain wall [296] beside perimeter wall [250], streets and the Room 92 block. A late 3C drain cut through earlier architecture. The source only proposes its connection to the gateway culvert, so that connection is retained as uncertain.
